_comment: Known tools: the name shown, other ways people write it, and the link each tool name opens (in a new tab). Tools not listed here link to a web search for their name. "category" is one of the ids in TOOL_CATEGORIES (lib/shape.js). "about" is one plain sentence shown in the tool's details. Only add links to the product's own site or repository.

tools.name: Claude Code
tools.about: Anthropic's coding agent. It works in your terminal and editor, reads the codebase and makes changes.

tools.name: Claude
tools.about: Anthropic's chat assistant, on the web, desktop and phone.

tools.name: ChatGPT
tools.about: OpenAI's chat assistant, on the web, desktop and phone.

tools.name: Cursor
tools.about: A code editor built around an AI assistant that can edit across files.

tools.name: GitHub Copilot
tools.about: GitHub's AI assistant: suggestions while you type, chat in the editor, and an agent on github.com.

tools.name: Codex CLI
tools.about: OpenAI's open-source coding agent for the terminal.

tools.name: Gemini CLI
tools.about: Google's open-source coding agent for the terminal.

tools.name: Windsurf
tools.about: A code editor built around an AI agent.

tools.name: MCP connectors
tools.about: Model Context Protocol servers. They let an assistant read and act in other tools, such as trackers, chat and logs.

tools.name: tmux
tools.about: A terminal multiplexer: several terminal sessions in one window, kept running in the background.

tools.name: cmux
tools.about: A terminal app for running many coding agents side by side, with a notice when one needs you.

tools.name: T3 Code
tools.about: An app that puts several coding agents behind one window.

tools.name: Diffity
tools.about: A diff viewer for reading and commenting on changes, then handing the comments back to the agent.

tools.name: agent-browser
tools.about: A command line browser for AI agents, so they can open and test web pages themselves.
